basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Records that a proposition was asserted, by whom and with what scope, not whether it is true.
One record holds one proposition; compound statements are split.
References evidence and assessments rather than owning them.
Unlike a fact-check, it does not deliver a verdict.

may: Register and normalise a claim statement.
Qualify scope and state calibrated confidence.
Bind evidence references and assert relations to other claims.
Transition claim status with recorded authority.
mustNot: Present an asserted claim as established fact.
Merge several propositions into one record.
Silently reinterpret a claim when a scheme changes.
Run verification or adjudication within this model.
Attribute a claim to a person who did not make it.
requiresHuman: Deciding on contested claims with legal or reputational consequences.

considerations: Claims about people can damage reputations; attribution must be accurate.
Recording a claim is not endorsing it, and interfaces must make this clear.
Misinformation can spread if claim status is unclear.

items: A claim has a statement, an asserting party, a time, a scope and a status.
Often confused with evidence, a fact-check verdict, a fact in a database and the document that carries it.
Spread of false claims shown without status.
Lost context when scope is dropped.
